title: Beef and Ale Pie
subtitle: Slow-braised beef under a short crust pastry lid
excerpt: Tender chunks of braised beef with mushrooms in a rich savoury gravy, topped with a golden pastry lid. This recipe uses beef stock in place of ale, keeping the deep flavour while making the dish accessible.
sourceNotes: Beef and ale pie is a pub classic across Britain and Ireland, with braised beef pies appearing in British cookbooks from the 18th century. The combination of braised beef and ale draws on long traditions of cooking cheaper cuts slowly in whatever liquid was on hand.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Assemble and bake the pie on the day.

content.text: This recipe uses beef stock in place of ale, which is not available in the ingredient list. The result is a deeply savoury braise that works just as well. Brown the beef in batches over high heat for the best colour and flavour in the finished filling.

Make the pastry first so it can chill. Rub the cold butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Add 3 to 4 tablespoons of cold water and bring together into a dough. Flatten into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Season the beef well. Brown it in batches in a large, heavy pan over high heat, turning once. Remove and set aside. Reduce the heat to medium and fry the onions, carrots, and garlic for 5 minutes. Add the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Return the beef to the pan with the mushrooms, stock, thyme, and bay leaves.

Bring to a simmer, cover with a lid, and cook over low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes until the beef is very tender. Remove the lid and simmer for a further 15 minutes to reduce the gravy. Remove the thyme and bay leaves. Season and leave to cool.

Preheat the oven to 180 C. Spoon the cooled filling into the roasting tin. Roll out the pastry on a floured surface to fit the top of the tin with a 2 cm overhang. Lay over the filling, pressing and crimping the edges to seal. Brush with egg wash and cut two small slits in the centre.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Pastry lid sinks into the filling
items.cause: Filling was too hot when pastry was applied
items.fix: Cool the filling before adding the pastry lid.

items.cause: Not cooked long enough or heat was too high
items.fix: Cook on very low heat and allow the full 90 minutes.

items.symptom: Pastry is soggy on the underside
items.cause: Steam from filling condensed onto pastry
items.fix: Cut steam slits before baking to let moisture escape.
